analyst: Manual analysis using Claude Opus 5.5 for verification and code analysis

servers.code_repo: https://github.com/grafana/mcp-grafana (open server; the cloud server at the CSV endpoint is not fully published)
servers.server_cost: Open server free. Cloud: each connected user counts as an "active AI user" of Grafana Assistant. Free plan: up to 3 active AI users/month (40M tokens each) + 25M tokens for service accounts, blocked above the limit. Pro: $20 per active AI user (40M tokens included), extra tokens $2 per 1M. Simple data queries consume no tokens, Assistant functions do.
servers.linked_cost: Grafana OSS free; Grafana Cloud Free $0, Pro from $19/month + usage, Enterprise from $25,000/year
servers.pricing: Cloud MCP is billed via Grafana Assistant (active AI users + tokens); see server cost. Grafana Cloud itself: usage-based tiers.
servers.restrictions: Grafana >= 9.0. Cloud: Grafana Cloud only, Assistant available on the stack, Assistant terms accepted; role "Assistant Cloud MCP User" (Editor+ by default); Write may need "Assistant Admin"; OAuth consent screen with Read / Query / Write levels (Write needs scope grafana:write). Rate limits not documented; default request timeout to Grafana 10 s.
servers.restricted_by: Grafana administrator (RBAC), server operator (flags --enabled-tools, --disable-write, --disable-query ...), user (cloud OAuth consent screen)
servers.governance_logic: 1) Operator modes: --disable-write (removes writing tools; grafana_api_request GET-only), --disable-query, category toggles (12 categories off by default). 2) The server classifies query languages by danger (SQL and InfluxQL count as writing). 3) Server instructions change with the configuration. 4) Unknown arguments rejected with a list of valid names; automatic type coercion. 5) Loki cost limiter (--loki-guardrail-mode off|shadow|enforce: selector, 24 h range, 100 GiB scan; rejects with a rewrite hint; off by default). 6) Enforced Loki matchers (the AI can only narrow; fail closed; warns about bypasses). 7) Response size limits (Loki 10 lines default, max 100, +1 line to signal truncation); economical dashboard tools. 8) HTTP security: Host/Origin checks, no cross-domain redirects, URL whitelist. 9) Required RBAC permissions declared in _meta, checked by Grafana (403). 10) Metrics/tracing; arguments in spans only with a flag. No human confirmation (cloud: only the OAuth consent screen).
servers.structure_note: Flat but modular: 34 categories switched on/off by flags; no hierarchy of sub-servers. Cloud: Tempo tools are proxied from the MCP servers of Tempo data sources. A universal tool (grafana_api_request) covers the whole Grafana API.
servers.actions_comment: 119 tools in the open code, 79 enabled by default; several are multi-operation; grafana_api_request reaches any API endpoint. Cloud server: list in the docs incomplete (by category), without grafana_api_request, plus Assistant tools.
servers.tokens: ~27,000 by default (79 tools ~26,600 + instructions ~460); ~40,000 with everything enabled
servers.token_method: Length of the reconstructed tools/list JSON / 4 characters per token (+-30 %)
servers.agent_cannot: With grafana_api_request (default): almost nothing beyond the token's RBAC rights; the real boundary is RBAC. Without it (or in the cloud server): no tools to delete dashboards, folders or data sources, to manage users, teams, service accounts and roles (admin tools read only), organisation settings, remove/disable plugins, change resource permissions. Browser-only: visual panel editing, Explore UI (agent can only get a deeplink or a panel image).
servers.docs_recs: Give the service account only the necessary permissions (Editor is "less restrictive"). Use --include-args-in-spans only outside production / without personal data. Do not expose the server without --server-auth-token; use TLS. For URL overrides deploy behind an authenticating proxy and restrict outbound network access. Disable bypasses (--disable-api, --disable-rendering, --disable-assistant) for Loki restrictions to work. Cloud: for read-only untick both Write and Query ("clearing only Write access still allows raw SQL"). No recommendations on human confirmation.
servers.gov_promises: Anonymous usage statistics ON by default (every 4 h: tools called, error counts, configuration; not arguments, queries, logs, credentials, instance URL; coarse region/network added from IP; opt-out --usage-stats=disabled or DO_NOT_TRACK=1). SQL: "credentials are never seen by the MCP server". Cloud: "Grafana doesn't train AI models on your PromQL, LogQL queries, investigation content, or prompt payload data"; LLM providers (Anthropic, Google Vertex AI, Amazon Bedrock) with zero retention; conversations kept 30/90/180 days (default 90); up to 30 days after deletion; employee access restricted and audited. Reversibility: dashboard versions exist, no one-command rollback; delete_annotation is "Permanently delete".
servers.user_promises: Feature list "for informational purposes only and does not represent a roadmap or commitment"; deeplinks "instead of relying on LLM URL guessing"
servers.promises_vs_logic: Statistics statements match the code (usagestats/), but on-by-default means data is sent without explicit consent. Loki restrictions are implemented and honestly documented together with their bypasses.
servers.notes: The CSV endpoint is the cloud server (separate hosted product, not fully published); the code analysis refers to the open server. Latest release tag v2.1.1. Actions sheet: tool list generated from the appendix 02b (type from readOnlyHint of all variants; description = first sentence of the verbatim description).

Tools.desc: 119 unique tools (34 categories), 79 enabled by default; some have read-only variants (grafana_api_request x3, generate_deeplink x2, agento11y_* x2). Every tool has annotations title/readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/idempotentHint/openWorldHint and _meta grafana.com/requiredPermissions.
Tools.post: Function result serialised to a JSON string in one text block; strings as is; get_panel_image returns PNG (base64). Some tools add AI hints (query_loki_logs: metadata on line count/truncation and hints for empty results).

Resources.desc: 3 HTML resources of MCP Apps (interactive UI inside the client): ui://mcp-grafana/panel-viewer.html, ui://grafana/metrics.html, ui://grafana/trace.html; linked to tools via _meta.ui.resourceUri

Prompts.desc: Not found in the code (no AddPrompt)

Logging.desc: No MCP log notifications; logs to stderr (slog) and optionally OpenTelemetry; slow-request log --slow-request-threshold

Authorization.desc: Open server: optional static Bearer token --server-auth-token for the MCP server itself (security error logged if missing on a non-loopback address); access to Grafana via service account token, login/password, Grafana Cloud on-behalf-of tokens, forwarded cookies/headers. No own OAuth server. Cloud: OAuth 2.1 in the browser; some clients need manual client ID/secret registration; consent screen with rights selection; token 1 h, auto-refresh for 30 days; revocation in Settings -> Connectors -> MCP clients.
Authorization.auth_server: Grafana (cloud); none in the open server
Authorization.src: README:453-459, 668-800; mcpgrafana.go:289-304; cloud-mcp docs; register-oauth-client docs

Elicitation.desc: Not found; alerting_rules_write contains the text instruction "Ask if context conflicts" (a request to the AI, not MCP Elicitation)

Tasks.desc: Not found; ask_assistant blocks the call until the answer (up to 5 min)

Configuration.desc: Dozens of flags and environment variables: categories, read-only, query-free, Loki restrictions, TLS, proxy, multi-organisation (--dynamic-multi-org adds orgId to every tool), statistics, --instructions-append

Error Reporting.desc: Tool error -> isError: true + text; unknown argument -> isError with the list of valid names ("self-correcting for LLM callers"); HardError / no authorization -> JSON-RPC error; panic -> internal error

Cancellation.desc: No explicit handling; handlers receive context.Context from go-sdk, through which the SDK can abort a request (not verified by running)

Other.desc: OpenTelemetry tracing incl. W3C trace context from request _meta; Prometheus metrics; anonymous usage statistics (on by default)

observations.text: The most "governed" of the first three servers: many server-side mechanisms (read-only/query-free modes, classification of query languages by danger, enforced filters, a cost limiter, URL whitelists).

A universal tool as a bypass of targeted restrictions: grafana_api_request ("Similar to 'gh api'") makes the other 118 tools convenient shortcuts; restrictions of individual tools do not work while it is enabled.
Responsibility is split: the server declares the required permissions (_meta), Grafana checks them. Security depends on how narrowly the administrator configured the token.
The server description for the AI depends on the configuration (dynamic instructions), so the same model sees a different "world" with different clients.
Context size as a design problem: about 27,000 tokens by default; the server addresses it with categories and economical tools.
Commercial model of the cloud version: every connected user counts as a paid "active AI user".
